name: Constitutionalism
summary: Constitutionalism holds that government can and should be limited in its powers by law that binds rulers and is hard for them to change. It pursues this through entrenched rights, the rule of law, separated and checked powers and often judicial review. It sits close to democracy, though critics argue that entrenched limits can override majorities.
scope: Liberal constitutionalism in the Lockean and American tradition (Locke, Montesquieu, the Federalist authors, Dicey) as described in the SEP entry: a theory of legal limits on power, not an economic or cultural programme, so most answers on those topics are neutral inferences. Excludes common-good and other minority strands except as noted.
